categories.title: 🧠 LLM Agentic OPD
categories.desc: On-policy distillation for language-model agents, tool use, planning, memory and long-horizon reasoning.
categories.desc_zh: 面向语言模型智能体、工具使用、规划、记忆与长程推理的在策略蒸馏。

categories.title: 🧩 Multimodal Agentic OPD
categories.desc: Agentic on-policy distillation for vision-language and other multimodal agents that perceive, reason and act.
categories.desc_zh: 面向视觉语言及其他能够感知、推理和行动的多模态智能体的在策略蒸馏。

categories.title: 🤖 Embodied Agentic OPD
categories.desc: On-policy distillation for vision-language-action models, world action models, robot navigation and manipulation, autonomous driving, and embodied code-as-policy agents.
categories.desc_zh: 面向视觉语言动作模型、世界动作模型、机器人导航与操作、自动驾驶及具身代码策略智能体的在策略蒸馏。

categories.title: 🎬 Video Agentic OPD
categories.desc: On-policy distillation for agents that understand, retrieve, reason over or interact with video.
categories.desc_zh: 面向视频理解、检索、推理与交互智能体的在策略蒸馏。

categories.title: 🔊 Audio Agentic OPD
categories.desc: On-policy distillation for speech, audio-language and voice-interaction agents.
categories.desc_zh: 面向语音、音频语言和语音交互智能体的在策略蒸馏。

categories.title: 🎨 Agentic Generative Systems (AGS) OPD
categories.desc: On-policy distillation for Agentic Generative Systems that plan toward goals, execute generation tools and refine outputs from feedback; generic iterative diffusion distillation is excluded.
categories.desc_zh: 面向 Agentic Generative Systems（AGS）的在策略蒸馏：系统围绕目标规划、调用生成工具，并依据反馈迭代改进输出；不纳入仅有迭代扩散蒸馏的工作。

papers.title: Capable Teacher, Myopic Scorer: Reward-Free Teacher Repair for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: In multi-turn agentic OPD, student departures can make next-token teacher scores unreliable even when teacher takeovers can still complete the task.
papers.q2: The paper diagnoses myopic scoring and develops reward-free teacher repair to make supervision more useful on difficult student states.
papers.q3: Evaluated on agentic long-horizon tasks; see the paper for the exact environments and student-teacher settings.
papers.q4: Repair quality depends on teacher capability and adds teacher-side computation.
papers.affiliation: NVIDIA

papers.title: ToolOPD: Credit-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Tool-Use Agents
papers.q1: Uniform teacher credit across long tool-use trajectories fails to identify the small number of actions that determine outcomes.
papers.q2: ToolOPD extracts hindsight skills from completed trajectories, converts outcome-sensitive teacher changes into action credit, and jointly reweights OPD with RL.
papers.q3: Long-horizon tool-interaction benchmarks with small language-agent students.
papers.q4: The method depends on outcome summaries and teacher probability access; the paper does not establish coverage beyond the evaluated tool tasks.
papers.affiliation: Northeastern University; Honor Device Co., Ltd.

papers.title: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Hierarchical teams receive only indirect final-answer feedback for intermediate search and answer agents.
papers.q2: A frozen teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens while RL supplies team and answer outcomes, jointly training a Leader-Searcher-Answerer system.
papers.q3: Seven question-answering datasets and four-attempt multi-agent solving.
papers.q4: The shared-parameter team and judge quality limit transfer to other agent organizations.
papers.affiliation: Alibaba Group; Zhejiang University

papers.title: Information-Gain Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Deep Search Agents
papers.q1: A search query that looks preferable before retrieval may return poor evidence, so token-level OPD can be blind to post-retrieval information utility.
papers.q2: The method uses information gain after retrieval to reallocate supervision across turns and calibrate query preferences.
papers.q3: Six multimodal search benchmarks, including MMSearch and BrowseComp-VL, with 2B and 4B students.
papers.q4: The calibration requires reliable retrieval utility and may depend on the search environment.
papers.affiliation: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen; Renmin University of China; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; BAAI

papers.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
papers.q1: Token-level OPD can suffer from state-distribution mismatch and requires teacher token probabilities and compatible tokenizers.
papers.q2: ActionOPD aligns semantic actions at student-visited states using sampled teacher actions, and Self-ActionOPD adds privileged same-model guidance.
papers.q3: Tool-use tasks with Qwen3 students and black-box or same-model teachers across four out-of-distribution benchmarks.
papers.q4: Action-level agreement may miss useful internal reasoning signals and depends on the action abstraction.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua University

papers.title: State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
papers.q1: In multi-turn agents, prior student reasoning can distort teacher targets while the current reasoning changes which actions are sampled at the same interaction state.
papers.q2: State-OPD grounds supervision in matched interaction states and allocates extra complete reasoning-action samples to high-entropy states.
papers.q3: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebShop with Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B students.
papers.q4: State matching and extra response sampling add rollout cost, and the reported environments are simulated.
papers.affiliation: Alibaba Group; Tsinghua University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; USTC

papers.title: Stochastic Teacher Intervention for Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Student actions change later observations, so multi-turn trajectories can drift away from the teacher distribution and make token supervision harmful.
papers.q2: STI-OPD samples teacher interventions from a KL-based discrepancy probability and uses importance-weighted reverse KL on the resulting mixed-policy trajectories.
papers.q3: Tool-integrated reasoning and long-horizon interaction benchmarks across multiple student sizes.
papers.q4: Interventions trade exploration for reliable supervision and require a calibrated discrepancy signal.
papers.affiliation: Monash University; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Zhongguancun Laboratory

papers.title: GraphOPD: Graph-Augmented On-Policy Distillation for LLM Agents
papers.q1: Teacher-student divergence is a poor credit signal in chained decisions because early drift contaminates later contexts.
papers.q2: GraphOPD builds a dependency graph from environment state changes and fuses graph-based structural credit with distributional disagreement.
papers.q3: ALFWorld, WebShop and SearchQA across three model scales and eleven baselines.
papers.q4: The method needs structured environment records and may be harder to apply to agents without explicit state transitions.
papers.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China; Xiaohongshu; HKUST (GZ)

papers.title: SCAD: Structured Credit Assignment and Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.q1: Sparse terminal rewards obscure intermediate contributions, while OPD can lose useful teacher guidance as student histories grow.
papers.q2: SCAD separates planning from bounded subtask execution, uses local execution distillation, and assigns planning credit through cross-rollout prefix trees.
papers.q3: Text and multimodal long-horizon agent benchmarks.
papers.q4: The decomposition and prefix-tree design may require task structure that is unavailable in arbitrary environments.
papers.affiliation: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; Tsinghua University; Nanyang Technological University

papers.title: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
papers.q1: When a fixed harness supplies context, tools and feedback, standard distillation imitates the teacher's full output instead of only the teacher capability missing from the harness.
papers.q2: HAD contrasts teacher actions with and without harness information after the student's own reasoning and filters invalid preference pairs.
papers.q3: Long-horizon agent benchmarks with a shared fixed harness.
papers.q4: The method assumes a stable harness and may not transfer when tool interfaces or feedback semantics change.
papers.affiliation: KAIST AI; Independent researcher

papers.title: Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: A student can outperform its teacher early in agentic OPD and then regress as continued distillation erodes successful student decisions.
papers.q2: The paper diagnoses distillation overshoot and proposes a selective protection mechanism for decisions that the student already executes successfully.
papers.q3: Agentic benchmarks and multiple teacher-student model families.
papers.q4: The protection criterion and its benefit depend on reliable decision-level outcome diagnostics.
papers.affiliation: University of Southern California; University of Florida; Emory University; University of Alabama; University of Maryland; Amazon AGI; Boston University; The Ohio State University; National Taiwan University

papers.title: PivotOPD: Learning to Recover from Pivotal Mistakes in Multi-Turn Agents
papers.q1: A single early action can make a later multi-turn rollout unrecoverable, while ordinary OPD treats all turns similarly.
papers.q2: PivotOPD identifies pivotal mistakes and focuses teacher guidance on recovery after the state-changing error.
papers.q3: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebShop with Qwen3 students.
papers.q4: Pivotal-error detection and recovery depend on the environment's notion of success and remaining budget.
papers.affiliation: Princeton University; NVIDIA; University of Maryland

papers.title: Teacher–Student Gaps Are Not Enough: Outcome-Guided On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Autonomous Agents
papers.q1: Large teacher-student distribution gaps can be benign, while small gaps can be outcome-critical in multi-turn autonomous agents.
papers.q2: OG-OPD weights teacher supervision by paired continuation outcomes rather than local distributional gap alone.
papers.q3: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebShop; the paper reports consistent gains over vanilla OPD.
papers.q4: Outcome pairing increases rollout cost and depends on reliable continuation evaluation.
papers.affiliation: Alibaba; Peking University; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

papers.title: Act First, Reason Later: Accelerating On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents via Reference-Conditioned Inverse Dynamics
papers.q1: Think-then-act rollouts delay environment interaction because long reasoning is generated before short actions.
papers.q2: ActFirst-OPD uses reference-conditioned inverse dynamics for quick actions, then asynchronously generates full responses for token-level teacher supervision.
papers.q3: ALFWorld, WebShop and ScienceWorld with Qwen3 students from 0.6B to 4B.
papers.q4: Reference transitions and asynchronous reasoning introduce additional data and scheduling assumptions.
papers.affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology; Zhongguancun Academy; Hong Kong Polytechnic University; DeepCybo; Nanyang Technological University

papers.title: DivOPD: Spread Wide, Look Close for Asynchronous On-Policy Distillation of Multi-turn Agents
papers.q1: Arrival-order batching in asynchronous OPD lets a few long rollouts dominate updates while other student interactions become stale.
papers.q2: DivOPD spreads a fixed turn budget across rollouts and prioritizes turns with cumulative teacher-student disagreement; optional teacher intervention handles no-progress episodes.
papers.q3: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebShop across six teacher-student settings.
papers.q4: Turn selection improves data use but still relies on usable teacher feedback and asynchronous infrastructure.
papers.affiliation: University of Chicago; Meituan; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; HKUST (GZ)

papers.title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents
papers.q1: Long-horizon multimodal search agents need deeper evidence gathering and process supervision than short multimodal questions provide.
papers.q2: MMSearch-OPD refines questions into harder search tasks and combines reward-guided RL with gap-weighted, decaying token-level OPD.
papers.q3: Multimodal deep-search benchmarks with image-question data and long evidence-gathering trajectories.
papers.q4: The refined task distribution and retrieval utility may limit transfer to other search engines or modalities.
papers.affiliation: Peking University; HKUST (GZ); Tsinghua University; The University of Hong Kong; Zhejiang University; Huawei Cloud

papers.title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: GUI agents need visual history for long tasks, but retaining screenshots is expensive and textual compression can discard state-critical evidence.
papers.q2: ECHOES recursively compresses history in a Compression-Think-Action format; privileged multi-image teachers distill student rollouts and balance OPD with task reward.
papers.q3: Four GUI benchmarks plus the ECHOESBMK perception-memory diagnostic benchmark.
papers.q4: Training uses privileged images and teacher updates that are unavailable at deployment.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua University; StepFun; Nanyang Technological University; Leapmotor; Honor

papers.title: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.q1: Flow-based VLA distillation faces distribution mismatch both in environment observations and in intermediate action-generation states.
papers.q2: The method couples student-driven environment rollouts with teacher velocity supervision along student-generated action-flow trajectories and combines multiple domain specialists.
papers.q3: LIBERO-40, CALVIN and Meta-World manipulation benchmarks.
papers.q4: Two-level flow supervision and repeated environment interaction may be costly for broader robot platforms.
papers.affiliation: Huawei Technologies; Tsinghua University

papers.title: JoyInside-VLM-Agent: Product-Conditioned Multimodal Policy Learning for Embodied Agents
papers.q1: Embodied agents must translate changing multimodal goals and execution feedback into actions under product constraints.
papers.q2: Staged SFT and multi-teacher OPD precede RL; DPER routes token-level evidence from a privileged teacher and privileged student through the rollout policy.
papers.q3: Robotic platforms and smart-hardware interaction tasks in a closed-loop sandbox.
papers.q4: Product-conditioned trajectory coverage and sandbox evaluation may not represent open-world embodiment.
papers.affiliation: JD.COM

papers.title: FastOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Lightweight VLA Deployment
papers.q1: Large VLA foundation policies are expensive to deploy, while few-step or compact policies can lose manipulation performance.
papers.q2: FastOPD combines flow-map teacher supervision with self-consistency to distill lightweight VLA students from foundation policies.
papers.q3: LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, World Action Model transfer and real-robot deployment.
papers.q4: Performance and latency depend on the teacher policy, flow parameterization and tested robot/task families.
papers.affiliation: KAIST; Sungkyunkwan University

papers.title: VISTA: Internalizing Collective Visual Experience via On-Policy Distillation for Active Multimodal Agents
papers.q1: Active multimodal agents collect complementary visual discoveries across interaction rollouts, but scalar RL advantages discard much of that information.
papers.q2: VISTA aligns observations from same-input rollouts with individual decisions and uses an experience-conditioned teacher to distill successful and failed trajectories.
papers.q3: Active visual-tool tasks and fine-grained perception/general reasoning benchmarks.
papers.q4: The approach assumes useful visual tools and may be sensitive to the diversity of same-input rollouts.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua University

papers.title: PIVOT: Pivot-Aware On Policy Self Distillation for Multi-Turn VLM Agents
papers.q1: Multi-turn VLM agents suffer sparse rewards and unrecoverable pivot actions that ordinary episode-level objectives cannot localize.
papers.q2: PIVOT uses visual trajectory diagnostics to locate pivot steps, re-score failed tokens with privileged context, and combine confidence-gated OPSD with GRPO.
papers.q3: Five multi-turn VLM agent tasks spanning grid puzzles, 3D control, navigation and generative reasoning.
papers.q4: The analyzer and teacher are training-time components, and pivot localization depends on task-specific rollback probes.
papers.affiliation: HKUST (GZ); IDEA; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University; Nanyang Technological University; Tsinghua University

papers.title: WAM-OPD: Sharpening World Action Models via On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Closed-loop world action models need fresh on-policy histories, making repeated real-robot rollouts expensive during distillation.
papers.q2: WAM-OPD uses prefix-weighted trajectory replay while refreshing denoising paths at student-visited histories and applying task-teacher supervision.
papers.q3: Simulated and real-world robotic manipulation adaptation with retained general skills.
papers.q4: Replay importance proxies approximate the changing history distribution and may fail under larger policy shifts.
papers.affiliation: USTC; Zhejiang University; Shandong Normal University; Tencent Hunyuan3D

papers.title: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
papers.q1: GUI agents trained on one platform can fail when action spaces, layouts and interaction conventions change.
papers.q2: UI-MOPD distills multi-platform GUI behavior on student-generated interactions to build a unified compact agent.
papers.q3: Multi-platform GUI benchmarks and cross-platform action prediction.
papers.q4: Platform diversity and visual grounding quality determine transfer.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua University

papers.title: Learn where to Click from Yourself: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
papers.q1: GUI grounding models need to learn reliable click locations from their own interaction distribution rather than only fixed demonstrations.
papers.q2: The method uses privileged GUI supervision to self-distill on-policy grounding decisions.
papers.q3: GUI grounding benchmarks and multi-turn mobile/computer interaction settings.
papers.q4: The method is tied to the available GUI action representation and platform screenshots.
papers.affiliation: IIE, CAS

papers.title: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.q1: GUI visual grounding errors persist at test time when the agent cannot use its own failed interactions as supervision.
papers.q2: Reflection-guided on-policy self-distillation turns test-time interaction feedback into grounding updates.
papers.q3: GUI grounding tasks with test-time self-evolution.
papers.q4: Online updates can accumulate errors and require safe interaction feedback.
papers.affiliation: Nanjing University of Science and Technology

papers.title: SOPD-SocialNav: Selective On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Social Navigation
papers.q1: Lightweight VLMs need social-navigation reasoning while large models are too expensive for onboard robots.
papers.q2: Teacher entropy selects socially informative decision tokens and a temperature-controlled JS objective distills student-visited navigation trajectories.
papers.q3: SNEI and MUSON benchmarks plus Scout Mini robot conversational and queuing scenarios.
papers.q4: The evaluation covers two benchmarks and limited real-world scenarios; selection depends on teacher uncertainty.
papers.affiliation: Hokkaido University

papers.title: VLA-OPD: Bridging Offline SFT and Online RL for Vision-Language-Action Models via On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: VLA training must bridge offline demonstrations and online interaction without destabilizing action policies.
papers.q2: VLA-OPD transfers teacher action distributions on student-visited observations before or alongside online RL.
papers.q3: Vision-language-action manipulation benchmarks; consult the paper for the exact environments and models.
papers.q4: The method depends on action-token calibration and simulated-to-real transfer.
papers.affiliation: HKUST (GZ)

papers.title: Refined Policy Distillation: From VLA Generalists to RL Experts
papers.q1: VLA generalists provide broad behavior while RL experts provide task performance, but directly combining their policies can be unstable.
papers.q2: Refined Policy Distillation transfers RL-induced policy changes back through on-policy student states to retain generalist behavior.
papers.q3: VLA manipulation tasks with generalist and RL expert policies.
papers.q4: The balance between generality and specialization depends on the task distribution.
papers.affiliation: University of Technology Nuremberg

papers.title: OWLET: On-Policy Weighted Learning via Evidence Transfer for Video Large Language Model Post-Training
papers.q1: Video-LLM post-training assigns coarse rewards or uniform OPD supervision even though different response tokens depend on different visual evidence.
papers.q2: OWLET transfers evidence-aware teacher signals and weights on-policy learning according to temporal visual support.
papers.q3: Video reasoning and understanding benchmarks with Video-LLM students.
papers.q4: Evidence attribution quality and long-video coverage constrain transfer.
papers.affiliation: USTC; Shanghai AI Laboratory; Tsinghua University

papers.title: Video-OPSD: Exploiting Privileged Visual Evidence for On-Policy Self-Distillation in Video Large Language Models
papers.q1: Video OPSD needs a privileged teacher that can isolate the frames supporting a student's long-video reasoning.
papers.q2: Video-OPSD conditions a self-teacher on evidence frames and weights token distillation by reliance on that privileged evidence.
papers.q3: Video understanding and reasoning benchmarks across multiple Video-LLM backbones.
papers.q4: Annotated evidence frames and long-video redundancy are required for the privileged teacher.
papers.affiliation: Nanyang Technological University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong

papers.title: Video-MOPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Video Understanding
papers.q1: Video understanding agents need complementary teachers for temporal perception and language reasoning on their own generated trajectories.
papers.q2: Video-MOPD combines multiple teacher signals with on-policy video-language distillation.
papers.q3: Video understanding benchmarks; exact teacher and model configurations are in the paper.
papers.q4: Teacher specialization and video sampling choices may limit generalization.
papers.affiliation: Tongji University

papers.title: Where to Look Matters: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Long-Video Understanding
papers.q1: Long-video agents must decide which temporal evidence to inspect, and uniform response supervision does not teach this selection well.
papers.q2: The method uses privileged or self-generated visual evidence to guide on-policy self-distillation for long-video reasoning.
papers.q3: Long-video understanding benchmarks with temporal evidence selection.
papers.q4: Results depend on evidence annotations or reliable self-teacher selection.
papers.affiliation: University of Maryland

papers.title: StreamOPD: A Post-Training Recipe with Spatio-Temporal Cue Gating for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.q1: Streaming video agents must process changing temporal context while standard OPD treats all generated tokens equally.
papers.q2: StreamOPD gates teacher guidance with spatio-temporal cues during on-policy streaming-video rollouts.
papers.q3: Streaming video understanding and temporal reasoning benchmarks.
papers.q4: Cue quality and streaming latency are central deployment constraints.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua University

papers.title: OPOD: On-Policy Omni Distillation
papers.q1: Pooled multimodal post-training can erase modality-specialist strengths, while multiple teachers provide conflicting guidance.
papers.q2: OPOD routes each student response to a modality teacher and applies selective confidence-aware on-policy guidance for text, image and audio.
papers.q3: Twelve multimodal benchmarks across three model scales.
papers.q4: Routing and confidence calibration must remain reliable as modalities and teachers grow.
papers.affiliation: Renmin University of China; Tencent

papers.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
papers.q1: Audio-language models lag text models in deep reasoning because high-quality audio-grounded reasoning trajectories are scarce.
papers.q2: X$^3$-OPD lets the audio student generate its own reasoning trajectories while a text teacher provides token-level guidance through matched inputs.
papers.q3: MMSU, MMAU, BIG Bench Audio and MMAR, including acoustic events and spoken dialogue.
papers.q4: Cross-modal transfer is limited when reasoning depends on information not recoverable from text.
papers.affiliation: Tencent Hunyuan; Zhejiang University

papers.title: Reward-Tilted On-Policy Distillation for Acoustic Grounding in Audio-Language Models
papers.q1: Audio-language students can answer from textual shortcuts while ignoring acoustic evidence.
papers.q2: RT-OPD contrasts teacher predictions with and without audio and uses the acoustic reward to reshape reverse-KL supervision on student responses.
papers.q3: Three audio-language benchmarks with compact students; the paper reports MMAU results.
papers.q4: The acoustic contrast depends on teacher sensitivity to audio and clean modality controls.
papers.affiliation: NEC Laboratories America; University of Connecticut

papers.title: TS-OPD: Reconciling ASR and QA in Speech Language Models via Task-Specific On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: ASR specialization can degrade the instruction-following and QA ability inherited by speech language models.
papers.q2: TS-OPD samples task-conditioned student trajectories and assigns ASR and QA teachers to their corresponding outputs.
papers.q3: Basic ASR, contextual ASR and QA evaluations.
papers.q4: Task-specific teachers and balancing coefficients may not cover mixed speech-agent workloads.
papers.affiliation: Nankai University; China Telecom Artificial Intelligence Technology Co.

papers.title: X-OPD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Distillation for Capability Alignment in Speech LLMs
papers.q1: End-to-end speech LLMs often lose the reasoning capabilities of their text-only counterparts.
papers.q2: X-OPD uses speech-student rollouts and a text teacher's token feedback to align multimodal representations and reasoning.
papers.q3: Speech-LLM reasoning benchmarks across multiple tasks.
papers.q4: Text teachers cannot directly supervise information unique to acoustics or prosody.
papers.affiliation: Tencent Hunyuan; Zhejiang University

papers.title: CORD: Bridging the Audio-Text Reasoning Gap via Weighted On-policy Cross-modal Distillation
papers.q1: Audio language models lose knowledge and reasoning relative to text models because audio-conditioned and text-conditioned representations diverge.
papers.q2: CORD performs token-level weighted reverse-KL and sequence-level reward optimization along audio student rollouts using an internal text teacher.
papers.q3: Audio reasoning benchmarks with 80K synthetic training samples.
papers.q4: The internal text teacher and synthetic speech coverage limit transfer to non-linguistic audio.
papers.affiliation: Baidu; Tsinghua University; Inner Mongolia University

papers.title: OmniOPSD: Rationale-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Affective Computing
papers.q1: Affective multimodal reasoning has sparse rewards and expensive rationale annotations, encouraging shortcut learning from labels.
papers.q2: OmniOPSD gives a same-model teacher frontier-generated evidence rationales as privileged context while the student samples from the original multimodal input.
papers.q3: MER-UniBench affective computing and human-centered multimodal reasoning.
papers.q4: Teacher rationale quality and human-centered scenario coverage determine robustness.
papers.affiliation: Shenzhen University; Tsinghua University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; USTC; Shenzhen Technology University; Tongji University; Huawei

papers.title: GenEvolve: Self-Evolving Image Generation Agents via Tool-Orchestrated Visual Experience Distillation
papers.q1: Open-ended image generation agents must search for evidence, select references and compose generation programs instead of mapping prompts directly to images.
papers.q2: GenEvolve compares best and worst tool-orchestrated trajectories and gives structured visual experience only to a privileged teacher for dense student distillation.
papers.q3: GenEvolve-Data, GenEvolve-Bench and public image-generation benchmarks.
papers.q4: Tool coverage and trajectory comparison quality affect self-evolution.
papers.affiliation: HKUST (GZ); Meituan; HKUST; National University of Singapore

papers.title: Skill-Decoupled On-Policy Expert Distillation for Unified Vision-Language Models
papers.q1: Jointly optimizing heterogeneous visual capabilities can create gradient interference and reward-hacking biases in a unified vision-language model.
papers.q2: SCOPED trains capability-specific experts, extracts reward-guided skills, and uses those skills only as privileged signals while on-policy-distilling the experts into one student.
papers.q3: Eight multimodal benchmarks with unified VLM students and independently trained capability experts.
papers.q4: The skill interface and expert coverage determine which capabilities transfer without exposing the skills at inference.
papers.affiliation: Northeastern University; Alibaba Group

papers.title: Do As I Do, Not As I Say: On-Policy Distillation Inherits the Teacher in Vision-Language Models
papers.q1: On-policy distillation can copy a teacher's persistent failure modes on student-visited visual states, even when filtered supervised fine-tuning would avoid them.
papers.q2: The paper compares OPD with filtered SFT under controlled teacher reliability and diagnoses how incomplete teacher responses alter student completion behavior.
papers.q3: ChartQA and Geometry3K across matched data budgets and teacher reliability conditions.
papers.q4: The conclusions depend on the selected VLM tasks and teacher settings, but provide a direct reliability audit for multimodal OPD.
papers.affiliation: Georgia Institute of Technology

papers.title: VC-OPD: Visual Counterfactual On-Policy Distillation for Grounded Vision-Language Reasoning
papers.q1: Uniform OPD weights template language and visually irrelevant continuations alongside tokens whose correctness depends on image evidence.
papers.q2: VC-OPD contrasts teacher predictions under the original and evidence-corrupted images, then uses the visual gap with mass-preserving normalization to reweight token-level OPD.
papers.q3: Multimodal visual-reasoning benchmarks with a teacher-supervised warm start and on-policy student trajectories.
papers.q4: Counterfactual image construction and teacher sensitivity determine whether the reweighting isolates useful visual dependence.
papers.affiliation: Tianjin University

papers.title: LEGO-OPD: Factorized Teacher Composition for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: A full VLM teacher distribution entangles language priors with visual grounding, so stronger visual supervision can damage language reasoning.
papers.q2: LEGO-OPD factorizes a language expert prior and a grounding expert likelihood, then composes them into a calibrated teacher distribution for OPD.
papers.q3: Multimodal reasoning benchmarks with language and vision experts supervising one student.
papers.q4: The factorization assumes separable language and grounding contributions and requires calibrated expert composition.
papers.affiliation: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Is Better Teacher Supervision Enough? Unlocking Student-side Learning in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Multimodal OPD can underuse improved teacher targets because the student policy itself fails to learn from dense supervision.
papers.q2: The paper analyzes student-side optimization bottlenecks and evaluates interventions that make teacher corrections more learnable on student rollouts.
papers.q3: Multimodal OPD experiments across visual reasoning tasks and teacher/student configurations.
papers.q4: The diagnosis is tied to the tested optimization and model families; stronger supervision alone is not a guaranteed fix.
papers.affiliation: Nanjing University; Fudan University; Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Distill the Visual Evidence, Not Just the Answer: Cross-World On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
papers.q1: A student can match a teacher answer while relying on different visual evidence, leaving grounded behavior implicit.
papers.q2: CW-OPD creates paired visual worlds with changed answer-critical evidence and distills the teacher's cross-world belief transition in addition to endpoint outputs.
papers.q3: Qwen3.5-4B experiments and the CWBench cross-world consistency diagnostic.
papers.q4: The method requires paired visual worlds and answer-changing evidence edits; coverage beyond those constructions remains open.

papers.title: On-Policy Visual Evidence Distillation
papers.q1: Visual agents interleave image operations and reasoning, so an early acquisition or reading error can corrupt all later evidence and answers.
papers.q2: ReVuE compares multiple student trajectories, diagnoses the first Acquire, Read, or Ground failure, and uses reflection-conditioned token reweighting for OPD.
papers.q3: Eleven visual-agent benchmarks across Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3.5 model families, including tool-use trajectories.
papers.q4: The reflection diagnosis adds rollout and teacher cost and depends on reliable failure-stage identification.

papers.title: Evidence-Aligned Multimodal On-Policy Self-Distillation for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding
papers.q1: Crop-conditioned teachers and lagged students introduce model-state and context changes that can contaminate visual corrections in OPSD.
papers.q2: EAD uses the current student's masked-versus-original prediction shift as an evidence reference and keeps only teacher corrections aligned with that visual direction.
papers.q3: Fine-grained visual-understanding benchmarks with crop-conditioned teachers and full-image students.
papers.q4: The alignment reference depends on meaningful evidence masks and adds paired student evaluations.
papers.affiliation: Beihang University; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Progressive-View On-Policy Distillation for Regional-to-Global Transfer in Multimodal LLMs
papers.q1: Crop-trained teachers see useful local evidence, but a full-image student must learn to use that advantage without a train-test view jump.
papers.q2: PVD gradually shifts the student from a crop to a padded crop and then the full image, with a regional-advantage weight for evidence-dependent tokens.
papers.q3: Visual perception, visual mathematics and general multimodal QA benchmarks.
papers.q4: The view curriculum and crop quality constrain transfer to images whose relevant evidence is not localized.
papers.affiliation: Baidu

papers.title: BAS-OPD: Budget-Aware Selective On-Policy Self-Distillation for Fine-Grained Multimodal Perception
papers.q1: Querying a privileged teacher for every multimodal rollout is expensive when only a subset of samples contains high-value visual supervision.
papers.q2: BAS-OPD keeps full-batch student generation but selects teacher queries with uncertainty, agreement and learned utility signals under a fixed budget.
papers.q3: Fine-grained multimodal perception benchmarks with controlled teacher-query budgets.
papers.q4: Selection quality and online utility estimates determine the cost-performance trade-off.
papers.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of California, Los Angeles

papers.title: CA-OPD: Confidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Structured Visual Prediction
papers.q1: Structured visual prediction needs dense correction, but low-confidence teacher tokens can inject unreliable geometry or label decisions.
papers.q2: CA-OPD calibrates token-level OPD with teacher confidence so that high-value structured visual corrections receive stronger supervision.
papers.q3: Structured visual prediction tasks with multimodal students and teacher confidence estimates.
papers.q4: Confidence calibration is task-dependent and may suppress useful corrections when the teacher is uncertain for the wrong reason.
papers.affiliation: Tianjin University; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Visual OPD usually needs a stronger teacher or privileged evidence, which is unavailable in fully self-supervised settings.
papers.q2: S²VOPD creates asymmetry by giving the on-policy teacher the original image while the student sees a task-consistent strongly augmented view.
papers.q3: Six fine-grained perception benchmarks with Qwen3.5-4B and controlled augmentation studies.
papers.q4: Augmentations must preserve task evidence; excessive removal creates a large but uninformative teacher-student gap.
papers.affiliation: Johns Hopkins University; University of Oxford; Georgia Institute of Technology; University of California San Diego; University of Maryland

papers.title: SkillLens: Visual Skill Cards for Retrieval-Augmented GUI Action Prediction and On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: GUI agents repeat long interaction patterns, while vanilla visual grounding does not expose reusable action skills to on-policy training.
papers.q2: SkillLens retrieves visual skill cards and uses them to guide GUI action prediction and on-policy distillation on student interactions.
papers.q3: GUI action-prediction and computer-use benchmarks with retrieved skill representations.
papers.q4: Skill-card retrieval coverage and platform-specific action semantics constrain transfer.
papers.affiliation: Peking University; ByteDance; Shanghai Jiao Tong University

papers.title: ADOPD: Reference-Privileged On-Policy Distillation for MLLM-Based Industrial Anomaly Detection
papers.q1: Query-only anomaly detectors miss fine deviations that become clear when a reference image is available during training.
papers.q2: ADOPD lets a reference-aware teacher score query-only student rollouts under matched and mismatched references, using reference-specific log-ratio signals.
papers.q3: MMAD industrial anomaly detection with zero-shot query-only inference.
papers.q4: Reference quality and industrial-domain coverage limit transfer beyond matched anomaly settings.
papers.affiliation: Zhejiang University

papers.title: OPD-V: Visual On-Policy Self-Distillation with Modality Balance
papers.q1: Text-heavy multimodal reasoning can ignore visual input even when the privileged teacher contains useful image evidence.
papers.q2: OPD-V contrasts zoom-in and masked-image teachers and distills only tokens inside a modality-balance trust region.
papers.q3: Six multimodal reasoning benchmarks with positive and negative visual teachers.
papers.q4: The mask and zoom views must preserve the intended modality contrast without removing task-critical context.
papers.affiliation: National Sun Yat-sen University; Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München; National University of Singapore

papers.title: VAD: Attributing Visual Evidence for Target Reconstruction in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Teacher corrections mix visual evidence with language priors and teacher-specific effects, obscuring which changes are actually visually supported.
papers.q2: VAD compares the same teacher with evidence present and removed, projects corrections onto the visual direction, and reconstructs a student-anchored target.
papers.q3: Six fine-grained visual benchmarks at 4B and 9B student scales.
papers.q4: Counterfactual evidence removal must isolate visual support; residual teacher information is treated only as a weak regularizer.
papers.affiliation: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xiaohongshu; Chinese University of Hong Kong; Zhejiang University

papers.title: OPLD: On-Policy Latent Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.q1: Token-level OPD does not directly constrain the latent reasoning states that accumulate visual evidence across multimodal chains of thought.
papers.q2: OPLD distills privileged multimodal reasoning into latent representations rather than only matching output tokens.
papers.q3: Multimodal reasoning benchmarks with latent-reasoning students and privileged multimodal teachers.
papers.q4: Latent alignment depends on representation interfaces and may not preserve interpretable evidence use.

papers.title: RP-OPSD: Resolution-Privileged On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multimodal Large Language Models
papers.q1: A low-resolution student can miss small visual details that a high-resolution teacher can inspect, creating a costly deployment gap.
papers.q2: RP-OPSD uses high-resolution privileged views to supervise low-resolution student rollouts while retaining the deployment input budget.
papers.q3: Multimodal large-language-model perception and reasoning benchmarks with resolution-controlled views.
papers.q4: The teacher resolution and visual encoder mismatch determine how much detail can be internalized.

papers.title: Med-OPD: Improving Medical Vision-Language Models via Evidence-Aware On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Medical VLMs can produce plausible clinical narratives from language priors while underusing diagnosis-critical image regions.
papers.q2: Med-OPD defines a medical evidence advantage from counterfactual teacher scoring and concentrates OPD on evidence-dependent tokens.
papers.q3: Medical vision-language benchmarks with evidence-aware post-training and zero-shot evaluation.
papers.q4: Clinical evidence hints and domain coverage must be validated before transfer to new medical datasets.
papers.affiliation: National University of Singapore; University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: H-OPD: Confidence Aware Heterogeneous Multi-Teacher Multimodal On-policy Distillation
papers.q1: A single teacher cannot reliably cover visual grounding and abstract reasoning at every token of a multimodal trajectory.
papers.q2: H-OPD arbitrates between vision-language and text teachers token by token using confidence and transferred visual semantics.
papers.q3: Eleven multimodal reasoning benchmarks with heterogeneous teacher pairs.
papers.q4: Teacher arbitration and visual-to-language transfer add calibration assumptions and inference-time teacher cost.
papers.affiliation: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; ByteDance

papers.title: V-Zero: Answer-Label-Free On-Policy Distillation with Contrastive Evidence Gating for Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
papers.q1: Answer-free visual reasoning needs trajectory-level discrimination, while dense OPD alone cannot tell whether a sampled rationale is evidence-grounded.
papers.q2: V-Zero pairs a relevant crop with a negative visual view and uses contrastive evidence gating to select answer-label-free OPD supervision.
papers.q3: Fine-grained visual reasoning benchmarks without annotated textual answers.
papers.q4: Negative-view construction must remain task-consistent; misleading crops can gate the wrong trajectory.
papers.affiliation: Sichuan University; Xi'an Jiaotong University; China Telecom; Peking University

papers.title: Seeing Before Reasoning: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Shortcut-Resilient Multimodal On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.q1: Multimodal students can reach answers through language shortcuts even when their perception of the image is wrong.
papers.q2: The method separates visual perception from reasoning during OPSD and distills a perception-sensitive signal before language reasoning updates.
papers.q3: Multimodal perception and reasoning benchmarks targeting visual shortcut behavior.
papers.q4: The decoupled interface may miss tasks where perception and reasoning must remain tightly coupled.
papers.affiliation: Shenyang Institute of Automation; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Visual-OPSD: Cross-Modal On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient Unified Multimodal Reasoning
papers.q1: Unified multimodal models often lose reasoning quality when visual and textual capabilities are optimized together.
papers.q2: Visual-OPSD uses cross-modal privileged views to provide dense self-distillation on student-generated multimodal reasoning.
papers.q3: Unified multimodal reasoning benchmarks with cross-modal teacher and student inputs.
papers.q4: Cross-modal privilege can transfer only information represented consistently across the paired modalities.
papers.affiliation: Xi'an Jiaotong University; Sun Yat-sen University

papers.title: Thinking Without Images: Internalizing Visual Manipulation with On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.q1: Repeated crop and zoom tool calls improve visual reasoning but make inference traces long and expensive.
papers.q2: Imagine-OPD gives a privileged teacher zoomed evidence while the student learns to imagine useful visual cues without invoking image tools at inference.
papers.q3: Vision-centric reasoning benchmarks comparing tool-using and internalized visual manipulation.
papers.q4: The student may hallucinate imagined cues when the training evidence distribution differs from deployment images.
papers.affiliation: Peking University; Central South University; University of Science and Technology of China; Huawei

papers.title: Teaching the Way, Not the Answer: Privileged Tutoring Distillation for Multimodal Policy Optimization
papers.q1: Sparse verifiable rewards give failed multimodal reasoning trajectories little token-level learning signal.
papers.q2: PTD-PO uses privileged spatial and intermediate-step hints to create dense teacher distributions without exposing the answer, then combines them with RLVR.
papers.q3: 2B–8B large vision-language models on multimodal reasoning tasks.
papers.q4: Privileged hints and the teacher-student context gap can introduce supervision that is unavailable at inference.
papers.affiliation: Tianjin University; Beijing Institute of Technology; Singapore Management University; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Xiaomi

papers.title: ViCuR: Visual Cues as Recoverable Privilege for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Answer-side privileged teachers can teach shortcuts because their supervision depends on signals the student cannot recover at inference.
papers.q2: ViCuR replaces answer privilege with query-related visual cues and learns a sink-token cue-recovery representation for the student.
papers.q3: Seven multimodal benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-2B and 8B students.
papers.q4: Cue extraction must identify evidence that is both useful and recoverable from the deployment image.
papers.affiliation: Fudan University; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; Nanjing University

papers.title: Decomposed On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Reasoning: Steering Gradients for Visual Grounding
papers.q1: Dense OPD gradients mix visual grounding with generic language continuation, diluting the updates that should change visual decisions.
papers.q2: The method decomposes the distillation signal and steers optimization toward visual-grounding directions on student trajectories.
papers.q3: Vision-language reasoning and visual grounding benchmarks.
papers.q4: The decomposition depends on a reliable visual-language partition and may be sensitive to gradient weighting.

papers.title: Visual-Advantage On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
papers.q1: Standard OPD may improve answers without making the student rely more on fine-grained visual input.
papers.q2: VA-OPD measures teacher log-probability changes with and without visual detail and reweights high-visual-advantage tokens at rollout and token levels.
papers.q3: Geometry3K, ViRL39K and six additional visual reasoning or understanding benchmarks across Qwen3-VL teacher sizes.
papers.q4: The visual-null control and teacher sensitivity determine whether the advantage isolates genuine visual supervision.
papers.affiliation: Institute of Automation; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; National Sun Yat-sen University; Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hospital

papers.title: Vision-OPD: Learning to See Fine Details for Multimodal LLMs via On-Policy Self-Distillation
papers.q1: Multimodal LLMs often miss small image details even when their language reasoning is strong.
papers.q2: Vision-OPD uses privileged visual views to self-distill fine-detail perception on the student's own generated responses.
papers.q3: Fine-grained multimodal perception and reasoning benchmarks.
papers.q4: Performance depends on how privileged views are selected and whether fine-detail gains transfer to full-image inputs.
papers.affiliation: Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Software; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Xiaohongshu

papers.title: OPD-Aha: From Linguistic Momentum to Visual Reflection in Multimodal On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: A mistaken early rationale can make teacher and student agree on the same visual hallucination, collapsing ordinary discrepancy-based supervision.
papers.q2: OPD-Aha isolates the teacher's real-image versus visual-null preference and reconstructs targets that encourage reflection before continuing the faulty rationale.
papers.q3: Fine-grained perception and multimodal reasoning benchmarks with reflection-aware trajectories.
papers.q4: Visual-null quality and reflection-token behavior affect whether the reconstructed target corrects or destabilizes reasoning.
papers.affiliation: Arizona State University; University of Virginia; Stevens Institute of Technology

papers.title: Learn How to Act from Your Own Interactions: On-Policy Self-Distillation for GUI Agents
papers.q1: Extending GUI OPSD from grounding to multi-turn interaction is limited by weak privilege following and insufficient memory guidance.
papers.q2: GUI-SD-v2 jointly trains privileged and unprivileged rollouts, then selectively distills step-specific reasoning and memory guidance from the self-teacher.
papers.q3: AndroidWorld and MobileWorld multi-turn GUI-agent benchmarks.
papers.q4: Privilege-following and memory selection are platform-sensitive and require training-time privileged states.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua University; Tencent; Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Information Engineering; Nankai University

papers.title: The Next Screenshot Knows: Gated Hindsight Distillation for Mobile GUI Agents
papers.q1: Offline GUI imitation discards the next screenshot even though it often reveals why the current action is correct.
papers.q2: GHD gives a parameter-sharing teacher the next screenshot and applies hindsight distillation only when it can recover a failed student action.
papers.q3: AndroidWorld and AndroidLab mobile GUI tasks with on-policy responses.
papers.q4: The hindsight screenshot is unavailable at deployment and the gate depends on reliable action recovery.
papers.affiliation: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Trust the Right Teacher: Quality-Aware Self-Distillation for GUI Grounding
papers.q1: Teacher coordinate signals become unreliable after a student prefix has already drifted away from the target element.
papers.q2: Quality-aware self-distillation gates teacher signals by whether the coordinate can still complete to the ground-truth box and scales them by confidence.
papers.q3: Six GUI grounding benchmarks with coordinate-token supervision.
papers.q4: The correctness gate uses ground-truth boxes during training and may not transfer to unseen action representations.
papers.affiliation: University of Georgia; Tencent; Hong Kong Polytechnic University

papers.title: Skill-Guided Continuation Distillation for GUI Agents
papers.q1: Policy-induced off-trajectory GUI states have no expert demonstration, leaving the agent without a correct continuation.
papers.q2: SGCD intentionally reaches off-trajectory states, then uses skill-guided successful continuations mixed with expert data to distill recovery behavior.
papers.q3: OSWorld-Verified across three GUI agent backbones.
papers.q4: Skill extraction and continuation quality govern whether the method recovers or reinforces off-trajectory errors.
papers.affiliation: University of Science and Technology Beijing; Nanyang Technological University; Tsinghua University

papers.title: Video-OPD: Efficient Post-Training of Multimodal Large Language Models for Temporal Video Grounding via On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Temporal video grounding receives sparse episode rewards even though each timestamp decision needs fine-grained evidence.
papers.q2: Video-OPD applies reverse-KL supervision to student trajectories and uses teacher-validated disagreement focusing to prioritize reliable informative rollouts.
papers.q3: Temporal Video Grounding benchmarks with multimodal large language models.
papers.q4: Teacher validation and disagreement selection add teacher computation and depend on reliable temporal evidence.

papers.title: Counterfactual Attention Policy Distillation for Temporal Video Grounding
papers.q1: Token-level video OPD does not reveal which temporal segments support a predicted timestamp in long videos with repeated actions.
papers.q2: CAPD masks temporal groups, measures the teacher distribution change, and uses counterfactual influence to weight timestamp-related distillation.
papers.q3: TimeLens and general video benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-8B students.
papers.q4: Temporal masking granularity and the teacher's attention response determine whether the influence signal is localized.
papers.affiliation: Xiamen University; Fudan University; Chinese University of Hong Kong; Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: MeSD: Multi-Evidence Self-Distillation for VideoLLM
papers.q1: A single teacher context can hide agreement and conflict between answer, temporal and spatial evidence in VideoLLM training.
papers.q2: MeSD uses shared-parameter evidence-specific teachers, fuses common and residual preferences, and routes success, failure and indeterminate trajectories differently.
papers.q3: Multiple video reasoning benchmarks with answer, temporal and spatial evidence teachers.
papers.q4: Evidence construction and verification labels add supervision cost and may not cover videos with missing annotations.

papers.title: Deep Thought Alignment: Trajectory-Level Latent Distillation for Video Reasoning
papers.q1: Output-token OPD does not constrain latent states that accumulate evidence across many video frames.
papers.q2: Latent-OPD distills end-of-trajectory hidden states and progressively aligns deeper teacher layers with student reasoning states.

papers.q4: Latent-layer matching adds memory and depends on compatible teacher and student representations.
papers.affiliation: Tencent; Fudan University

papers.title: OP-CAD: On-Policy Clean-Audio Distillation for Robust Audio-Visual Reasoning
papers.q1: Environmental noise and competing speech can corrupt audio-visual reasoning while standard OPD treats all response tokens similarly.
papers.q2: OP-CAD trains a corrupted-audio student against a clean-audio teacher and uses clean, corrupted and visual-only contrasts to select token supervision.
papers.q3: Audio-visual question answering under progressively stronger environmental noise.
papers.q4: Clean-audio privilege and curriculum severity determine robustness outside the tested noise conditions.
papers.affiliation: Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School; Tsinghua University

papers.title: DriftOPD: Sequence-Level Reverse-KL Distillation for One-Step VLA Policies
papers.q1: Chunk-level VLA training ignores how a current action changes long-horizon task success, while closed-loop sequence RL is costly for real robots.
papers.q2: DriftOPD decomposes sequence reverse-KL into chunk and future-potential terms and optimizes them with a one-step drift objective and an offline critic.
papers.q3: Simulation and real-world manipulation across multiple VLA architectures.
papers.q4: The method relies on an offline Q-function and assumes its future-potential estimate remains useful under policy drift.

papers.title: Reflect-VLA: Internalizing Reflective Guidance via Dual-Path On-Policy Self-Distillation for Autonomous Driving
papers.q1: Scalar driving rewards identify that a trajectory is poor but do not diagnose whether perception, behavior selection or execution caused the error.
papers.q2: Reflect-VLA treats reflective diagnoses as privileged information, distilling corrective distributions on risky rollouts while self-imitating reliable trajectories.
papers.q3: Autonomous-driving VLA planning with long-tail scenarios and dual-path OPSD.

papers.title: RE-0: Verified Recursive Improvement of Embodied Code-as-Policy Agents through Local On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: A stronger teacher can still fail on particular embodied states, so global imitation can assign credit to harmful corrections.

papers.title: WAM-OPD: Joint Video-Action Supervision for World Action Model Post-Training with On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: World Action Models generate future video and robot actions, but ordinary post-training supervises only one output on histories encountered by the student.

papers.q4: Paired teacher video-action queries and simulator-to-robot coverage determine generalization.

papers.title: ROAD-VLA: Robust Online Adaptation via Self-Distillation for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.q1: Sparse rewards provide weak supervision for high-dimensional autoregressive action policies during online VLA adaptation.

papers.title: FORCE: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Fine-Tuning via Value-Calibrated Warm-up and Self-Distillation
papers.q1: VLA RL can suffer catastrophic early unlearning and waste updates on low-value exploratory actions.
papers.q2: FORCE calibrates a Q-function with on-policy warm-up, then filters policy and expert actions and uses self-distillation to stabilize online fine-tuning.

papers.title: On-Policy Distillation of Language Models for Autonomous Vehicle Motion Planning
papers.q1: Large language models for motion planning are expensive on board vehicles, while small students must learn from states induced by their own waypoint outputs.

papers.title: SnapFlow: One-Step Action Generation for Flow-Matching VLAs via Progressive Self-Distillation
papers.q1: Flow-matching VLA action chunks require many sequential solver evaluations, limiting control frequency.

papers.title: CV-OPD: Contrastive Vision On-policy Distillation
papers.q1: A multimodal student can answer correctly after visual regions are masked, showing that ordinary OPD can improve answers without teaching genuine visual reliance.

papers.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
papers.q1: MLLMs need spatially grounded visual guidance, but human grounding annotations and external teachers make privileged multimodal OPSD expensive.

papers.title: SCOPD: Sparse-Context On-Policy Self-Distillation for Efficient Vision-Language Models
papers.q1: Extreme visual-token pruning leaves useful evidence available but makes the student use it unreliably under a sparse context.

papers.title: Distill What the Student Can See: Fisher-Projected On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
papers.q1: A compact VLM may be unable to realize every visual correction in a full teacher distribution, so stronger targets can reduce downstream performance.

papers.title: MOPDA: Mixed-Trajectory On-Policy Distillation for Language-Guided Industrial Anomaly Detection
papers.q1: Industrial anomaly agents must turn language judgments into pixel localization, but standard trajectory supervision does not expose evidence-conditioned visual states.

papers.q1: Aggressive visual-token compression sharply reduces multimodal performance even though some task-relevant evidence survives in the sparse representation.

papers.title: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation
papers.q1: Self-distillation needs teacher-student asymmetry, but answer or privileged-evidence annotations are costly and can create shortcuts.

papers.title: Frame Differential On-Policy Self-Distillation for Video Reasoning

papers.q2: FD-OPSD compares sparse- and dense-view teacher preferences on the same student response and distills the frame-differential signal without an external teacher.
papers.q3: Six video-reasoning benchmarks with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-4B across frame budgets.
papers.q4: The dense-view reference is available only during training and its benefit depends on frame selection.
papers.affiliation: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: DeepSearch-World: Self-Distillation for Deep Search Agents in a Verifiable Environment
papers.q1: Long-horizon web agents need dense self-improvement signals, while fixed teacher trajectories and sparse rewards limit search-policy evolution.
papers.q2: DeepSearch-Evolve iterates trajectory generation, verification, filtering, mixing and self-distillation inside a deterministic verifiable search environment.
papers.q3: DeepSearch-World with 420K multi-hop QA tasks and BrowseComp, GAIA and HotpotQA evaluation.
papers.q4: The self-evolution loop depends on deterministic tools and verifiable task outcomes.
papers.affiliation: HKUST Shenzhen Research Institute; HKUST (GZ)

papers.title: SD-Search: On-Policy Hindsight Self-Distillation for Search-Augmented Reasoning
papers.q1: Outcome rewards assign the same credit to every search query even though only some queries determine whether a trajectory succeeds.
papers.q2: SD-Search conditions a same-model teacher on hindsight summaries of grouped rollouts and distills its query preferences back to the inference-time student.
papers.q3: Search-augmented reasoning agents with query-level supervision layered on GRPO.
papers.q4: Hindsight summaries and grouped-rollout outcomes must reliably identify useful search decisions.
papers.affiliation: Kuaishou

papers.title: OPD-Evolver: Cultivating Holistic Agent Evolver via On-Policy Distillation
papers.q1: Memory systems can store experience without teaching an agent how to select, use, write and maintain reusable knowledge.
papers.q2: OPD-Evolver uses a slow-fast co-evolution loop and privileged hindsight to distill four memory-management abilities into a deployable policy.
papers.q3: Multi-domain agent-evolution benchmarks with hierarchical memory operations.
papers.q4: The memory hierarchy and outcome attribution determine which experiences become reusable skills.
